posts.text:
🚨 JUST IN: Rep. Tim Burchett just FIRED BACK at John Thune reportedly trying to BLOCK his appointment to the US Senate by Governor-elect Marsha Blackburn (TN), per @toddstarnes 

"I LOVE the fact that he's not for me!" 

🔥🔥

Burchett says a prominent media figure told him Thune "had sent the word out that he does not want me, because I would not do what leadership told me to do."

His response: "You know what? You're EXACTLY RIGHT."

"The big boys are not for me. The big, big players in the party, the one or two that pull a lot of the strings, that write the big checks, they're not for me. They've never been for me. They're always for me the day after the election."

Keep being FOR THE PEOPLE, @timburchett 

Burchett has said he'll just run for the seat anyway if he's not appointed.

NOTE: This is NOT Blackburn giving indication as to who she'd appoint. It's ENTIRELY up to her — her Senate seat, and her governorship!

Hopefully she goes with Burchett, he's a good man 🙏🏻

posts.text:
Reported details on why Skydance removed James Gunn & Peter Safran as co-heads of DC Studios:

• 'Supergirl' was viewed as a box office disaster

• Superman’s $618M box office was not impressive to Skydance — it reportedly lacked pop culture impact to them

• DC heads were reportedly reluctant or slow to share future DC plans, slate details and footage with Skydance execs

• They wanted to report directly to David Ellison to maintain strong control over the rollout of DC projects

• One insider says the exec shakeup has been in the works since early Fall

• Gunn and Safran will still have direct links to the studio, but with less control

• It is unclear if Gunn will get the chance to finish any of his vision for Superman, which reportedly includes a trilogy

• One DC insider expressed concern about whether fans will continue investing in the franchise if it is rebooted yet again

(via @THR)

🇺🇸 🇨🇳 China’s AI stocks just crashed 40% in four months... and every American with a 401(k) is sitting on the same bet.

Jaspreet Singh, founder of Minority Mindset and CEO of Briefs Media, says 83% of S&P 500 companies are at least 10% off their highs, and the index only keeps setting records because a few AI giants, mostly trading the same money back and forth, are carrying it:

“Our economy today is so propped up on AI that if AI spending slows down... we would be in a recession.”

Anyone in an index or target date fund is already in that bet, and most have no plan for the day it breaks.

@MinorityM1ndset

🇸🇦 🇨🇳 🇮🇷 🇺🇸 Iran was selling 90% of its oil to China... and the rest of the Gulf is now leaning the same way.

Simon Dixon, founder of BnkToTheFuture, says the shift was underway long before this war, with China now the biggest buyer of Gulf energy, Iran and the UAE already in BRICS, and Saudi Arabia hedging as an observer:

“So now what is feeding what used to feed the Gulf countries was private corporate interests in America. Now it’s being fed by China.”

If the Gulf’s biggest customer keeps sitting in Beijing, its money will follow, and the petrodollar loses another leg.

@SimonDixonTwitt

🇺🇸 What turns an ordinary dip into a full CRASH? Borrowed money and the margin call that comes with it.

Jaspreet Singh says investors buying stocks on debt get forced out by their brokers once prices slide, which drags markets even lower, and that’s what just happened in China and South Korea.

He points to 2008, when Fed hikes made adjustable mortgages unaffordable, as proof of what usually ends the party:

“What we’ve seen generally is the needle that pops the economic bubble is higher interest rates.”

With the Fed holding at 3.75% to 4% and markets betting on a December hike, that needle is closer than it looks.

@MinorityM1ndset

🇮🇱 🇺🇸 Israel’s debt is climbing and its credit rating has been cut... while its defense and tech stocks keep booming.

Simon Dixon says the war is draining nation states while the companies around them cash in, naming Palantir, Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics and Raytheon as winners, with Saudi Aramco posting a 36% jump in profits:

“That’s private interest benefiting while state interest is being depleted.”

The longer this war drags on, the more governments pay for it and the more the contractors pocket.

@SimonDixonTwitt
